_comment: The capability-footprint ratchet, measured 2026-07-30. Built BEFORE the carve
it instruments, so the migration is measurable from its first commit rather
than from whenever somebody notices it needs a number.
SUBJECT: the transitive `ambition_*` closure a consumer links by depending on
the facade alone. docs/concepts/api-growth.md records why a clean facade
can hide this — 'a perfectly semantic API could still force a movement-only
game to compile and link menus, persistence, audio, LDtk, bosses and every
unrelated gameplay domain'. No consumer names a forbidden path; the footprint
is still wrong.
⚠ ONE invariant here, not two. The set may not GROW. It deliberately does NOT
require pruning as it shrinks, because unlike the module allowlist there is no
'slot' to reoccupy — a crate leaving the closure cannot be silently replaced
by a different one without the count moving. Stating the difference because
the other two ratchets DO need both halves and copying them blindly here
would add a rule with no failure behind it.
ZERO unwanted means a game links only what it asked for. That is the
condition §4's carve exists to reach.

2026-08-01: `ambition_geometry` added, and it is NOT a widening. The crate was CARVED OUT of `ambition_platformer2d_core`, which was already in this closure — the same shapes/boxes/reference-frames code, now behind its own name. The ratchet was right to stop on a new name; the architecture changed on purpose, so the baseline moves in the SAME COMMIT rather than the contract being waived. The number that would mean something is the consumer linking code it did not already link, and this is not that.

2026-08-02 — baseline moved by the `ambition_projectile_spec` carve. ADDED ['ambition_projectile_spec']; REMOVED []. The ratchet stopped this change and was right to: a new crate genuinely entered the consumer's closure. It is recorded rather than waived, which is what that check's own message asks for.

⚠ HONEST COST: this carve makes the sentinel's closure BIGGER by one crate, not smaller. What it bought is elsewhere — `ambition_vfx` now builds with `ambition_platformer2d_core` absent from its closure entirely (measured with `cargo tree --edges normal`), the first crate for which that is true after four earlier carves that only removed a DECLARED edge. A consumer that links the whole facade pays one more compilation unit; a consumer that wants only the effect vocabulary now stops at four general-named crates.

2026-08-09 — baseline moved by the `ambition_character_sprites` carve (D33). ADDED ['ambition_character_sprites']; REMOVED []. The ratchet stopped it and was right to: a new crate name genuinely entered the sentinel's closure. ⚠ NOTHING NEW IS LINKED — the code is the animation pickers, the sheet-authored body geometry and the manifest attack hitbox, all of which the sentinel already compiled inside `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith`. What changed is that they answer upward now: the actor crate does NOT depend on this crate, so an edit to a sprite derivation no longer rebuilds 112k lines of unrelated actor code. A carve that had left the registration behind would have put it BELOW the actor crate instead and bought none of that — see the D33 row.

2026-08-17 — baseline moved by the `ambition_conversation` carve (D33 step 2). ADDED ['ambition_conversation'] to the closure AND to `never_asked_for`; REMOVED []. The ratchet stopped it and was right to: a new crate name genuinely entered the sentinel's closure. ⚠ NOTHING NEW IS LINKED — this is the conversation-continuity authority, ledger, hold and break rule that had been compiling inside `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` since it was written; the monolith depends on it unconditionally, so the same code arrives by the same route under its own name. ⭐ it joins `never_asked_for` rather than the wanted half, and that is the honest entry: a movement-only game asked for neither dialogue nor conversation, and `ambition_dialog` and `ambition_ui_nav` were already counted unwanted for exactly this reason. ⛔ so the count reads 16 where it read 15, and the carve did NOT cause that — it NAMED it. The number that would mean something is a consumer linking code it did not already link, and this is not that. Shedding it needs the capability to become optional at the monolith's edge, which is the §4 obligation, not this move.

2026-08-17 — baseline moved by the `ambition_boss_encounter` carve (D33). ADDED ['ambition_boss_encounter'] to the closure AND to `never_asked_for`; REMOVED []. The ratchet stopped it and was right to: a new crate name genuinely entered the sentinel's closure. ⚠ NOTHING NEW IS LINKED — this is the boss data model, catalog, phase tick, encounter entity and reward chests that had been compiling inside `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` since they were written; the monolith depends on it unconditionally, so the same code arrives by the same route under its own name. ⭐ it joins `never_asked_for`, which is the honest half: a movement-only game asked for no bosses, and `ambition_encounter` was already counted unwanted for exactly that reason. ⛔ so the count reads 17 where it read 16, and the carve did NOT cause that — it NAMED it. What it bought is elsewhere: 7,635 lines left the largest compilation unit in the workspace, and the boss domain now answers upward, so a boss edit no longer rebuilds 114k lines of unrelated actor code. Shedding it from the closure needs the capability to become optional at the monolith's edge — the §4 obligation, not this move.
why_the_split_matters: The second list can be closed by making facade edges optional — a manifest change. The first cannot: a game that needs actors needs `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith`, which brings them. That is what makes the footprint irreducible without moving code, which is §4's carve condition.

facade_only_four_are_not_a_quick_win.finding: The four crates reachable ONLY through the facade's own edges — inventory_ui, touch_input, portal_presentation, render — are named through `ambition::` by in-repo code 49, 12, 19 and 90 times respectively. 170 call sites.
facade_only_four_are_not_a_quick_win.why_it_matters: The split recorded above says 15 of 19 unwanted crates need the carve and 4 are 'fixable by making them optional'. True, and it undersells the four: making an edge optional means cfg-gating its re-export, which means every one of those 170 in-repo call sites must either sit behind the same feature or gain it. `render` alone is 90, and `presentation` and `game_assets` are built on it, so gating it is really gating the visible face.
facade_only_four_are_not_a_quick_win.so_the_honest_scope_is: A facade-optionality slice, not a manifest tweak. It is still worth doing and still measurable by this ratchet — 19 -> 15 is a real number — but it is a migration with consumers, and calling it cheap was wrong.
facade_only_four_are_not_a_quick_win.how_this_was_caught: By counting the call sites before starting, rather than after. The earlier 'fixable by making them optional' was inferred from the dependency graph alone, which shows what depends on what and not how much of the tree says its name.

slice_h_remeasurement.how: cargo tree --edges normal in the sentinel's own workspace, which is now also how the ratchet measures (a static manifest walk counts optional edges the sentinel never enabled, so the counter could never move).
slice_h_remeasurement.\u26a0_render_did_not_leave_and_that_is_: The edge IS optional now, but `minimal_game`'s own slice-B exit criterion composes the windowed face (`the_minimal_game_boots_windowed`), and the windowed face draws. Per the slice-H spec's failure-mode clause, a feature the sentinel needs to keep passing its tests is not optional FOR IT: the manifest names `ambition_render` and the closure keeps it. A game with no windowed face drops it — the edge is measured as cuttable, just not by this sentinel.
slice_h_remeasurement.\u26a0_audio_resisted_for_a_different_re: Declaring SILENCE is an audio-catalog registration (`ModuleDraft::no_audio` registers an `AudioCatalogFragment`), so the composition path needs `ambition_audio` even for a soundless game — and it arrives via `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` regardless, so gating the facade edge would have cut nothing. Left unconditional.
slice_h_remeasurement.the_remaining_15_wait_on_the_carve: Every crate still in `never_asked_for` is in `reachable_via_ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith_alone`; no facade manifest change can remove them, which is exactly the §4 carve condition this file has recorded since it was first measured.

\u26a0_ambition_binding_is_a_SPLIT_not_a.what_changed: The binding-resolution boundary (`Resolver` / `Bound` / `Namespace` / `BindingLedger` / `BindingReport`) left `ambition_platformer2d_shared_tangle::binding` for its own crate, `ambition_binding`, whose entire dependency list is `tracing`.
\u26a0_ambition_binding_is_a_SPLIT_not_a.why_the_ratchet_had_to_move: This counter asks whether a movement-only game gained a CAPABILITY it never asked for. It did not: `ambition_binding` is a strict subset of a crate already in the closure, so the sentinel links exactly the code it linked before, in one more node. 41 -> 42 here is a decomposition, and the number this file exists to defend — `never_asked_for`, 15 — is UNCHANGED.
\u26a0_ambition_binding_is_a_SPLIT_not_a.why_it_was_worth_a_node: The boundary is generic Rust and `shared_tangle` is ~18k lines across 51 files of platformer lifecycle, camera, transit, schedules and hotkeys. `ambition_characters` — the canonical character domain — depended on all of it for ONE name, so an edit to any of those 51 files invalidated it. The edge was legal and the absence contracts passed; legality is not the same question as floor (GPT 5.6 review of `1579ab3`, finding 3).
\u26a0_ambition_binding_is_a_SPLIT_not_a.\u26d4_what_this_note_must_NOT_be_used_f: A crate that adds behaviour to the closure is a growth and this ratchet should go red for it. The test is whether the new node is code the sentinel was ALREADY linking under a different name. If it is not, do not copy this entry.

ldtk_left_the_closure_2026_08_22.what: ambition_platformer2d_ldtk (and third-party bevy_ecs_ldtk) left the movement-only sentinel's closure: 44 -> 43, never_asked_for 17 -> 16.
ldtk_left_the_closure_2026_08_22.how: Three edges, not one. The runtime named the LDtk crate UNCONDITIONALLY (its own `LdtkWorldPlugin` and one `Option<LdtkRuntimeIndex>` slot on PreparedPlatformerSource) -- that edge is `optional` now behind a `ldtk` feature forwarded through the provider and the facade, and folded into `all_capabilities`. The other two were the hard-coded monolith feature lists this file's row already named: ambition_sim_view asked for `ldtk_runtime`+`portal` and ambition_platformer2d_runtime for `portal_ldtk`, and the monolith's ldtk dep is optional-but-enabled by exactly those.
ldtk_left_the_closure_2026_08_22.why_it_could_be_done_now_and_not_in_augu: D136 probed dropping those two lists on 2026-08-18 and recorded that the MONOLITH itself did not build without `ldtk_runtime`. Re-probed 2026-08-22: it does (`--no-default-features --features visible`, zero errors). The cfg-gating landed in between; the recorded blocker outlived it.
ldtk_left_the_closure_2026_08_22.\u26a0_the_content_fingerprint_did_not_m: The provider writes `world.runtime-index` from the installed index; without the capability a game has none, and an absent index writes byte-for-byte what a RON-authored game already wrote (one `area\t<id>\t\t-` row per room). That equality is stated in the provider's own comment and is why this is a link-closure change, not a content-identity change.
ldtk_left_the_closure_2026_08_22.portal_followed_the_same_day: ambition_portal2d left too: 43 -> 42, never_asked_for 16 -> 15. FOUR unconditional edges (monolith, runtime, sim_view, and ambition_projectiles) plus the runtime's ungated `ambition_portal2d::register_rollback_state`, which is now behind `portal` exactly as the LDtk row is. The portal CODE was already cfg-gated everywhere; only the manifests said otherwise. ⚠ and making the dep optional exposed a feature-unification lean: `ambition_projectiles::diagnostics` uses `bevy::prelude::info` and was getting `bevy_log` through ambition_portal2d's bevy features. It names the feature itself now — a crate that needs a feature declares it.

settings_menu_left_the_closure_2026_08_2.what: ambition_settings_menu left the movement-only sentinel closure: 42 -> 41, never_asked_for 15 -> 14.
settings_menu_left_the_closure_2026_08_2.how: Two ownership leaks were removed together. ambition_game_shell no longer imports the full settings/system-menu IR to edit four universal audio fields; its private row identity delegates to the canonical AudioSettings mutation helpers already in ambition_persistence. ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith no longer names ambition_settings_menu only to forward its dev_tools feature; the public facade weakly forwards ambition_settings_menu?/dev_tools instead, so developer tooling configures that capability when selected without selecting it.
settings_menu_left_the_closure_2026_08_2.why_this_is_not_a_monolith_carve: No actor code moved. The monolith had zero source references to ambition_settings_menu; its edge existed only as feature forwarding. Removing that composition responsibility and the independent shell edge is enough for the crate to leave a narrow consumer.
settings_menu_left_the_closure_2026_08_2.runtime_behavior: Rich/default compositions still select ambition_settings_menu through all_capabilities. Enabling dev_tools still enables the settings menu developer row when the settings capability is present. Narrow compositions retain the shell audio controls because those mutate UserSettings::audio directly through AudioSettings helpers.

mount_entered_the_closure_2026_08_26: ⭐ DECLARED GROWTH, not a leak. `ambition_mount` is the MOUNT PAIR carved out of the actor monolith (D33): the monolith's construction and spawn roads BUILD pairs, so every consumer of the monolith links the crate that owns them. ⛔ EXACTLY the shape `ambition_boss_encounter` already has in this list, and for the same reason — a carved domain the composition still names. ⚠ the carve did NOT make the footprint worse in substance: the same code was linked before, inside the monolith. What changed is that it is now COUNTABLE, which is what this ratchet is for. ⇒ the way out for both is the same and neither has it yet: a movement-only game should not install the domain's plugin, and the closure should follow the installation rather than the dependency.
damage_entered_the_closure_2026_08_26: ⭐ DECLARED GROWTH, and the same shape as the mount row above. `ambition_damage` is victim-side damage resolution carved out of the actor monolith (D33); every consumer of the monolith links it because the monolith's own actor and boss damage roads call into it. ⚠ the same code was linked before, inside the monolith — what changed is that it is COUNTABLE, which is what this ratchet is for. ⭐⭐ AND THE CARVE MADE AN INVISIBLE EDGE SAY ITSELF: the module reads gameplay settings for the assist-mode damage scale, so `ambition_damage` names `ambition_persistence`. That cost nothing to notice while it lived in a crate that already had it, and a damage resolver depending on a settings store is worth someone's judgement. ⇒ the way out is the mount row's, and neither has it: the closure should follow the plugin a game INSTALLS, not the dependency its crate declares.
